notes: Size: 277 operators, all gated (no ungated rule), plus 9 keyword extensions. This is far above the 20-60 guideline because the bank's failures are almost all distinct named concepts: 212 operators each solve their own bank or regression item (209 bank items newly solved). The other 65 have no bank item of their own; they are same-concept variants of a solving operator (inverse direction or decoding, other traversal order, other output shape, or the unrounded form of a formula whose rounded form solved the item). They are marked '(no bank item of its own: same-concept variant)' in this report and can be retired as a group if only bank-solving rules are wanted; none was written from memory of a benchmark task. Regression: BROKEN 0; 7 regression items that were solved by coincidental programs (1-019, 1-027, 1-104, 1-132, 1-218, 1-248, 1-250) are now solved by the named rule (rotate, ISBN-10, acronym, h-index, alternate merge, cancel pairs, version sort). Robustness checks in scratch_pilot/: (a) 190 re-phrasings of solved bank items in my own wording (paraphrase_bank*.json, judged by the same asserts): 190/190 solved; (b) 34 simple negative-control tasks whose descriptions contain words my gates react to, which the library solved before: no program changed. Every emitted template was tested on edge cases (empty input, ties, negatives) in edge_tests.py. Risks: predicates that are False on almost any input could fit a False example by accident when their gate opens; their gates are kept to phrases (one such case, 'HH:MM' opening is_valid_time, was found and fixed). Broader gates that remain: windows (window/sliding), closest_value (closest|nearest with target words), missing_between ('missing', list output only), modes ('most common', list output only). Engine ideas: (1) when a description asks for rounding to k places, prefer programs that end in round(..., k): an exact visible value lets the unrounded formula win and fail the hidden tests (Imag/1-003, 1-183 are ternary formulas, where the rounded-variant workaround used here would need four arguments); (2) quaternary operators (1-107, 1-152); (3) the named_pairs feature would solve differences of two named derived values such as two parsed clock times (1-151). Rounded variants accept only 0-4 places because other numbers in such descriptions are part of the formula ('* 5 / 9').
